title: Variable Scope & Lifetime
focus: local vs package vs global scope, block scoping, short vs long declaration
rules: CountDeclarations returns the number of distinct variables you declare
ShadowExample should demonstrate understanding of block scoping

flashcards.front: What is the difference between := and var in Go?
flashcards.back: := is short variable declaration, only works inside functions. var works anywhere and can declare package-level variables.

flashcards.front: What is the scope of a variable declared with := inside a function?
flashcards.back: Block scope — it's only visible within the nearest curly braces { } where it was declared.

flashcards.front: Can you redeclare a variable with := in the same scope?
flashcards.back: No, := requires at least one new variable on the left side. You can shadow in inner scopes though.

flashcards.front: What is a zero value in Go?
flashcards.back: The default value when a variable is declared without initialization: 0 for numbers, '' for strings, false for bools, nil for pointers/slices/maps/channels/interfaces.
